mina: Heads-up — after bringing marlin-v1 through int8 onboarding we see a ~7% chrF drop on our JP->ZH testset. suspiciously localized to lines that mix dots/hyphens and fullwidth punctuation :eyes:
yuki: Can you paste a minimal repro example? Also which quant kernel?
mina: Quick paste: source and two outputs (fp16 vs int8)
```
Source: 東京都·臺北—テスト・チェック-例
FP16 detokenized: 東京都·臺北—テスト・チェック-例
INT8 detokenized: 東京都·臺北-テスト･チェック-例
```
(changed U+2014 em-dash vs hyphen-minus and U+00B7 middle dot vs U+30FB katakana middle dot)
cheng: hmm looks like boundary shifting between CJK and kana sequences. tokenstream differs, not just detok. likely normalizer or tokenizer table differences combined with quant-induced subtokenization drift.
sam: infra note: int8 kernel sometimes takes a different packing path that slightly changes the effective chunking for K/V caching; that can shift greedy decoding alignment in rare mixedscript sequences. we saw similar with long mixed tokens cause different tokenization seam. :shrug:
yuki: I ran the tokenizer locally against that exact string, here's tokens from our onboard test harness:
```
FP16 tokens: ["東","京","都","·","臺","北","—","テ","ス","ト","・","チェ","ック","-","例"]
INT8 tokens: ["東","京","都","·","臺","北","-","テ","ス","ト","･","チェ","ック","-","例"]
```
so the middle dot / hyphen mapping toggles, causing downstream detok mismatch and small translation shifts.
cheng: two hypotheses: (1) input normalizer maps U+30FB vs U+00B7 differently depending on locale flags at tokenization time; (2) quantized tokenizer weights or piece selection rounding changed the subword split. more likely (1) because token ids differ before model decoding.
mina: CI diffs show chrF drop concentrated in samples with interleaved JP/KR/HAN and punctuation. sample count ~420/12k.
ci-bot: test-run marlin-v1-int8-smoke 4940001250: chrF baseline=0.642, int8=0.597, regression count=418, top-1 culprit pattern="mixeddot-hyphen"
yuki: Quick mitigation — canonicalize punctuation in preprocess to NFKC and map both middle dots to U+30FB, map em-dash to fullwidth hyphen if present. simple script patch in tokenizer preproc: 
``` 
# normalizer pseudo
s = s.replace('\u00B7', '\u30FB')
s = s.replace('\u2014', '\uFF0D')
```
sam: If we do that, need to sync across hosted and private tokenizers and add a small canary to ensure no perf regression. I can roll a deduped config flag: `tokenize.canonicalize_punct=true` for canary pools.
cheng: Also add a unit test asserting token stability pre/post quant: `assert tokens_fp16 == tokens_int8` for canonicalized inputs. put sample strings in tests/locale/ambig_punct.txt
yuki: ran the canonicalizer locally — tokens align and chrF delta goes to +0.002 on the mini-bench. promising.
mina: OK plan: (1) small normalizer patch + unit tests (2) config flag for canary rollout (3) run full smoke and diff report; merge only when chrF stable. assigning owners: yuki normalizer PR, cheng tests, sam canary rollout. pinging @sam for infra schedule. :thumbsup:
sam: scheduled canary for tonight 02:00 UTC, will route 5% of int8 traffic to canary. CI will auto-collect metrics.
mina: thanks — keep updates here. if we still see bleed after canonicalization we escalate to kernel/packing investigation. :eyes:
